scope: Backend-only durable file-call and per-operation claims through embedded xlang3/SQLite
verified: Exact generation, process identity, ordinary root, workspace, revision and latest finished actual model tool call authorize one file invocation
Both read and file claim keys preserve opaque 256-byte Unicode provider call IDs; the key format remains unchanged for prior valid identities
The read-only canonical turn explicitly rejects unsupported file tools before looking up read claims
Invocation entry and approved native mutation claims are separate; native operations must already be executing with matching run, workspace, revision, folder and operation kind
Each native operation has a unique private model/invocation/spec binding; duplicate, changed or replacement calls cannot replay it
Injected transaction failure rolls back operation binding, invocation update and event together
Exact output bytes and digest are retained; success requires known successful native effects and partial failure preserves prior successful operations
Lease retirement preserves unresolved ownership; late native results remain recordable without dispatch authority
Private claim/effect categories reject generic information access; active calls participate in deletion and quiescence checks
SQLite restart preserves returned, partial and unresolved claims; serial build and 61 focused contracts pass with frozen input and binary sets
limitations: New file-ledger cases use synthetic process/model/proposal identities; they perform no filesystem mutation
The separate existing native file-host test still covers actual mutations and approvals, but is not yet composed with these durable worker claims
No file RPC endpoint, mixed canonical tool turn or production coding worker is enabled; process-read remains read-only
No new full-suite, installed, hosted, rendered or live-provider acceptance
